Map abundance profiles with a self-organizing map

gly_som.Rd

Train an unsupervised self-organizing map (SOM) and assign each profile to its closest grid unit. Training favors similar prototypes at neighboring units.

Usage

gly_som(
  exp,
  on = "variable",
  grid = NULL,
  topology = "rectangular",
  rlen = 100L,
  scale = TRUE,
  seed = 1L,
  add_info = TRUE,
  log_transform = NULL
)

Arguments

exp

A glyexp::GlycomicSE() or glyexp::GlycoproteomicSE() object, or another SummarizedExperiment containing an expression matrix and sample information.

on

Axis to map. "variable" maps each glycan or glycoform across the supplied samples. "sample" maps each sample across variables.

grid

Grid dimensions as two positive integers, c(xdim, ydim). By default, the map is square with side length min(5, floor(sqrt(n_train))), where n_train counts usable profiles.

topology

Arrangement of the grid units, either "rectangular" (default) or "hexagonal".

rlen

Number of training epochs. Each epoch makes as many online updates as there are training profiles.

scale

Whether to center and standardize each input coordinate across the retained profiles, as in gly_kmeans(). With at least two training profiles, each sample (variable map) or variable (sample map) is centered at its mean and divided by its sample standard deviation. Constant coordinates are centered at zero. A single profile is used directly.

seed

Nonnegative integer seed for initialization, online training and tie breaking. The default restores the caller's random-number state after fitting, as does any supplied integer. Use NULL to draw from the caller's random-number stream.

add_info

Whether to attach annotations for the mapped axis.

log_transform

NULL (default) uses metadata(exp)$scale to avoid logging data twice. TRUE requests the method's log transformation for raw data; if the input is already on "log", "log2", "log10", or "logx", it warns and uses the supplied values unchanged. FALSE always uses the supplied values unchanged. This argument must be named when it follows ....

Value

A glystats_som_res object inheriting from glystats_res. get_tidy_result() returns a tibble in input order with one row per mapped-axis ID (.variable or .sample for SE inputs).

  • unit, x, and y identify the winning unit and its grid coordinates.

  • distance is the Euclidean distance to that unit's fitted prototype in the training coordinates. Smaller values indicate a closer fit.

  • n_finite counts finite coordinates. Excluded profiles retain their IDs and receive missing assignments and distances. exclusion is "no_finite_values" or "incomplete_profile" for these profiles and NA for the training profiles.

diagnostics contains n_train, units (occupancy of every grid unit, including empty units), and quantization_error (mean training distance). get_raw_result() returns the kohonen::som() fit with its training data, fitted assignments, codebook vectors, and per-epoch changes. With zero usable profiles, the automatic grid is empty, quantization error is missing, and the fit is NULL. An explicit grid requires at least one usable profile per requested unit.

settings records the axis, grid dimensions, topology, epochs, standardization request and seed. preprocessing records the abundance transformation, whether standardization was applied (scaled), and the IDs of wholly non-finite coordinates (excluded_coordinates). The result retains the input meta_data and SE identifiers.

Details

The columns of the input assay represent individual samples. To map group-average curves, first supply an experiment with one column per group mean. Each supplied coordinate contributes to Euclidean distance. Standardization gives each varying coordinate equal variance. With scale = FALSE, coordinates with larger spreads can dominate the map. With relative abundances, a change in one glycan's share can affect the shares of other glycans. Distances describe similarity relative to the normalization reference and depend on the abundance transformation.

Raw assays use log2(x + 1e-6) by default. See gly_scale for other scales and overrides. On the analysis scale, coordinates with no finite values are removed first. Training uses profiles with finite values at every remaining coordinate. A complete flat profile is eligible because its level contributes to distance. Initial grid prototypes are sampled without replacement from the training profiles. Changing the grid or seed can change the assignments, and unit numbers are local to each fit.

References

Kohonen T (1982). Self-organized formation of topologically correct feature maps. Biological Cybernetics, 43, 59-69. doi:10.1007/BF00337288 .

kohonen on CRAN.

Examples

exp <- glyexp::real_experiment2
res <- gly_som(exp, grid = c(2, 2), seed = 42, add_info = FALSE)
head(get_tidy_result(res))
#> # A tibble: 6 × 7
#>   .variable                unit     x     y distance n_finite exclusion         
#>   <chr>                   <int> <int> <int>    <dbl>    <int> <chr>             
#> 1 Hex(3)HexNAc(3)            NA    NA    NA    NA         138 incomplete_profile
#> 2 Hex(3)HexNAc(7)            NA    NA    NA    NA          94 incomplete_profile
#> 3 Hex(5)HexNAc(2)             2     2     1     2.46      144 NA                
#> 4 Hex(6)HexNAc(4)NeuAc(2)    NA    NA    NA    NA         136 incomplete_profile
#> 5 Hex(4)HexNAc(3)            NA    NA    NA    NA         143 incomplete_profile
#> 6 Hex(5)HexNAc(4)dHex(2)     NA    NA    NA    NA          64 incomplete_profile
res$diagnostics$units
#> # A tibble: 4 × 4
#>    unit     x     y n_profiles
#>   <int> <int> <int>      <int>
#> 1     1     1     1          2
#> 2     2     2     1          7
#> 3     3     1     2         11
#> 4     4     2     2          8
